text: Tokens sold in an ICO are structurally different from equity: they do not generally confer ownership rights, no right to dividends, and no claim on company assets in bankruptcy, so the risk and reward profile of a token is not that of a share.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615

isBasedOn.name: Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags

abstract: Risks and rewards of tokens differ from those of equity. Unlike token ownership, equity typically conveys a right to dividends. In the case of bankruptcy, equity owners have some claims on the assets of the company.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: comparison of ICOs to initial public offerings
